tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List every RankAuthority project (website) the caller owns or is an accepted member of.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description:
Get one RankAuthority project's details: domain, platform, scan/recommendation counts, CMS status.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID), from list_projects.

tools.name: list_keywords
tools.description:
List the active tracked keywords for a project.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: list_keyword_suggestions
tools.description:
List AI-suggested keywords awaiting approval for a project.

        To act on a suggestion, use approve_keyword_suggestions /
        reject_keyword_suggestions rather than this read-only listing.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: add_keywords
tools.description:
Add and start tracking one or more keywords for a project.

        Mirrors the app's "Add Keyword" action for a batch: each new keyword
        charges the project's keyword budget and queues DataForSEO metric
        tracking (Search Volume, CPC, current rank), which completes
        asynchronously after this call returns. Pass a single-item list to add
        just one.

        Duplicates (case-insensitive) — already tracked or repeated within the
        list — are skipped, not errors. Keywords beyond the remaining plan
        budget are reported in ``skipped_no_budget``.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            keywords: Keyword phrases to track (1 or more).

tools.name: delete_keywords
tools.description:
Stop tracking and delete one or more keywords for a project.

        Pass a single-item list to delete just one. Keywords that already fed a
        generated blog cannot be deleted and are reported in ``blocked``;
        unknown ids land in ``not_found``. Each successful delete refunds one
        keyword slot to the plan's monthly allowance.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            keyword_ids: Keyword ids (UUIDs) to delete — see list_keywords.

tools.name: approve_keyword_suggestions
tools.description:
Approve AI-suggested keywords, moving them into active tracking.

        Approving charges the project's keyword budget (same as add_keywords)
        and queues the same DataForSEO metric tracking for each approved
        keyword.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            suggestion_ids: Specific suggestion ids to approve (see
                list_keyword_suggestions), or omit to approve all pending
                suggestions.

tools.name: reject_keyword_suggestions
tools.description:
Reject AI-suggested keywords, deleting them without charging the budget.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            suggestion_ids: Specific suggestion ids to reject (see
                list_keyword_suggestions), or omit to reject all pending
                suggestions.

tools.name: list_recommendations
tools.description:
List a project's SEO recommendations, grouped by status.

        Returns approved/archived/declined/resolved/deleting/deleted
        buckets (newly-generated, not-yet-reviewed recommendations aren't
        included here — see get_recommendations_count for the full status
        breakdown, including "new"). To approve a recommendation use
        approve_recommendation / approve_all_recommendations; publishing the
        approved fix to the live site happens via an async snippet-regen job
        (no separate "publish" step in the app for this either).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            sub_category: Optional filter, e.g. "keyword-cannibalization".
            search: Optional case-insensitive text search over the recommendation content.

tools.name: get_recommendations_count
tools.description:
Get recommendation counts by status/sub-category for a project (dashboard summary).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: approve_recommendation
tools.description:
Approve a single SEO recommendation.

        Approving only marks intent, same as in the app — the live CMS/site
        picks up the change via an async snippet-regen job, it isn't a
        separate "publish" step you need to trigger.

        Args:
            recommendation_id: The recommendation's id (UUID) — see list_recommendations.

tools.name: approve_all_recommendations
tools.description:
Approve every pending SEO recommendation for a project (optionally filtered).

        Same as the app's "Fix All" button. Approving only marks intent — the
        live site picks up approved fixes via an async snippet-regen job.

        keyword-cannibalization is never auto-approved here: fixing it rewrites
        live keyphrases across multiple pages and requires choosing which page
        keeps the keyword, so that always needs human review in the app (this
        call returns a refusal with a deep link instead of approving).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            sub_category: Optional filter, e.g. "title" or "schema-markup".
                Omit to approve everything (including schema markup).

tools.name: get_integration_status
tools.description:
Check which CMS/analytics integrations are connected for a project.

        Returns a connected bool per provider (wordpress, shopify, wix,
        webflow, gohighlevel, gsc) plus an app_links block pointing every
        disconnected provider at the Integrations page. Google Search Console
        and WordPress can start browser authorization via MCP; integrations
        that require pasted credentials must be connected in the app.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: start_gsc_connect
tools.description:
Start a Google Search Console connect flow for a project.

        This only returns a Google consent URL — it does NOT complete the
        connection. The human user must open the URL in a browser and finish
        Google's sign-in/consent screen themselves; there is no way to
        complete this flow programmatically. After they finish, call
        get_integration_status to confirm gsc is connected.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: start_wordpress_connect
tools.description:
Start the WordPress auto-install connect flow for a project.

        Returns a URL to the site's WP admin "Authorize Application" page.
        This does NOT complete the connection — the human user must open the
        URL in a browser and approve the authorization themselves. After
        they finish, call get_integration_status to confirm wordpress is
        connected. Only works for websites detected as WordPress; other
        platforms should use their browser setup tool or get_app_link.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: start_gohighlevel_connect
tools.description:
Get the secure browser link for GoHighLevel setup.

        This does not change any integration state. The human user must open
        the RankAuthority Integrations page and complete setup there; the AI
        cannot request or receive credentials in chat.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: start_webflow_connect
tools.description:
Get the secure browser link for Webflow setup.

        This does not change any integration state. The project owner must
        open the RankAuthority Integrations page and complete setup there; the
        AI cannot request or receive credentials in chat.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: start_shopify_connect
tools.description:
Get the secure browser link for Shopify setup.

        This does not change any integration state. The project owner must
        open the RankAuthority Integrations page and complete setup there; the
        AI cannot request or receive credentials in chat.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: start_wix_connect
tools.description:
Get the secure browser link for Wix setup.

        This does not change any integration state. The project owner must
        open the RankAuthority Integrations page and complete setup there; the
        AI cannot request or receive credentials in chat.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: get_app_link
tools.description:
Get a deep link into the RankAuthority web app for a fenced-off action.

        Call this whenever the user asks for something this MCP surface
        doesn't expose as a tool — immediate publishing, entering integration
        credentials, disconnecting an integration, running a fresh scan,
        bulk actions, or an AI keyword search — then present the returned URL
        so they can finish the action in the app.

        Args:
            action: One of "blog_publish", "rankfast", "aiv_artifact",
                "ranklink", "integrations", "scan", "ai_keyword_search",
                "direct_visibility".
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID) to scope the link to.

        Returns:
            {"url": ..., "instructions": ...} on success, or
            {"error": ..., "known_actions": [...]} if `action` is unrecognized.

tools.name: list_blogs
tools.description:
List a project's blog posts (paginated, newest first).

        Covers both blogs and AI Visibility artifacts (``Blog.type``), draft
        through published. Generating new blog content is done via the
        generate_blog tool; scheduling a draft's publish date is done via
        schedule_blogs / schedule_aiv_artifacts. Publishing immediately is an
        in-app action — see get_app_link("blog_publish", ...).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            status: Optional filter — "draft", "scheduled", "published",
                "consolidated", or "archived".

tools.name: get_blog_generation_status
tools.description:
List a project's in-progress blog generation queue items.

        Only returns rows still pending/started/generating — once a blog
        finishes generating it moves out of this queue and shows up in
        list_blogs instead.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: list_rankfast_pages
tools.description:
List a project's RankFast campaigns (pages with generated content).

        Returns every RankFast row that already has generated content
        (new/pending/approved/scheduled/published/archived), newest first.
        Generating RankFast content for a fresh page is done via
        generate_rankfast; publishing or scheduling an existing draft is done
        in the app — see get_app_link("rankfast", ...).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: get_rankfast_counts
tools.description:
Get RankFast campaign counts by status for a project (dashboard summary).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: get_aiv_dashboard
tools.description:
Get the AI Visibility dashboard for a project: latest record + persona/topic/prompt counts.

        Immediate publishing of a generated GEO artifact is done in the app —
        see get_app_link("aiv_artifact", ...). Generate a new artifact with
        generate_aiv_artifact, or schedule one with schedule_aiv_artifacts;
        call get_generation_quota first to check the remaining article budget.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: list_aiv_prompts
tools.description:
List a project's active AI Visibility prompts (the queries GEO artifacts answer).

        These are the prompts you can grow with add_aiv_prompts — a good AI-
        assisted workflow is to draft new buyer-intent prompts yourself and add
        them here. Personas and key topics are managed only in the app.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: add_aiv_prompts
tools.description:
Add one or more AI Visibility prompts to a project (plain insert; no AI cost).

        Each new prompt consumes one slot from the plan's AIV prompt budget.
        This does NOT run any AI generation — draft the prompt text yourself (or
        with the assistant) and add it. Pass a single-item list to add just one.
        To generate a GEO artifact from prompts, use generate_aiv_artifact.

        Duplicates (case-insensitive) — already present or repeated within the
        list — are skipped and reported in ``skipped_duplicates``, not errors.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            prompts: The prompt/query texts to track (1 or more).
            related_topic: Optional topic label applied to every added prompt.

tools.name: delete_aiv_prompts
tools.description:
Delete one or more AI Visibility prompts from a project.

        Pass a single-item list to delete just one. Each successful delete
        refunds one prompt slot. Prompts already linked to a generated artifact
        or blog cannot be deleted and are reported in ``blocked``; unknown ids
        land in ``not_found``.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            prompt_ids: The prompt ids (UUIDs) to delete — see list_aiv_prompts.

tools.name: get_dv_dashboard
tools.description:
Get the latest Direct Visibility run summary for a project.

        Direct Visibility measures how often LLMs cite the site in response
        to real queries. "market" track uses top keywords by AI search
        volume; "content" track uses the project's own AI Visibility prompts.
        Run a fresh scan with run_direct_visibility_scan.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            track: "market" (default) or "content".

tools.name: get_dv_trend
tools.description:
Get historical Direct Visibility runs for a project (trend chart data).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            track: "market" (default) or "content".
            limit: Max number of most-recent runs to return (1-24, default 6).

tools.name: get_dv_queries
tools.description:
Get per-query citation results for a Direct Visibility run (defaults to the latest run).

        Content-track results are enriched with the linked blog's publish
        state (content_status, scheduled_date, published_date).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            track: "market" (default) or "content".
            run_id: Specific run id (UUID) to inspect; omit for the latest run.

tools.name: get_ranklink_dashboard
tools.description:
Get the RankLink dashboard for a project: silo/proposal/page counts.

        Discovering new silos is done via start_ranklink_discovery; publishing
        an approved silo's internal links to the live CMS is done in the app —
        see get_app_link("ranklink", ...).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: list_ranklink_silos
tools.description:
List a project's RankLink silos (topic clusters + orphan-recovery groups).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: get_ranklink_discovery_status
tools.description:
Get the most recent RankLink silo-discovery run's status (for polling).

        Does not include the discovered silos themselves — call
        list_ranklink_silos once the run's status is "completed".

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: get_generation_quota
tools.description:
Get a project's remaining generation quota across every content domain.

        ALWAYS call this before offering to generate a blog, RankFast page,
        or AI Visibility artifact, so you can tell the user up front if the
        relevant quota is exhausted instead of letting generate_* fail. Each
        domain's ``remaining`` is the exact count the app itself enforces
        (no separate math here) — 0 means generation for that domain will be
        rejected until the quota resets.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: generate_blog
tools.description:
Generate a new blog post for a keyword. SPENDS BLOG QUOTA and triggers
        paid AI generation (queued, completes asynchronously).

        Call get_generation_quota first to check the remaining blog budget. This
        tool itself is safe to call with confirm left at its default (false) —
        it only returns a preview (quota + today's cap) without generating
        anything. Confirm the spend with the user, then call again with
        confirm=true to actually queue generation. The finished draft can be
        scheduled with schedule_blogs; immediate publishing stays in the app,
        see get_app_link("blog_publish", ...).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            keyword: The keyword/topic to write the blog post about.
            keyword_id: Optional id of an existing tracked Keyword row to associate.
            confirm: Must be true to actually generate; false (default) previews.

tools.name: generate_rankfast
tools.description:
Generate RankFast content for chosen blog pages. SPENDS RANKFAST QUOTA
        and triggers paid AI generation (queued, completes asynchronously).

        Call get_generation_quota first to check the remaining RankFast budget.
        Leave confirm at its default (false) to preview (quota + today's cap)
        without generating anything; confirm the spend with the user, then call
        again with confirm=true to actually dispatch generation.
        Publishing/scheduling the finished content is NOT available here —
        that's done in the app, see get_app_link("rankfast", ...).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            page_ids: Page ids (UUID, see list_rankfast_pages / the app) to
                generate RankFast content for. Non-blog or unknown ids are
                skipped, not errored.
            confirm: Must be true to actually generate; false (default) previews.

tools.name: generate_aiv_artifact
tools.description:
Generate one AI Visibility (GEO) article for a prompt. SPENDS ARTICLE
        QUOTA and triggers paid AI generation (queued, completes asynchronously).

        Call get_generation_quota first to check the remaining AIV article
        budget (quota.aiv.article). Leave confirm at its default (false) to
        preview (quota + today's cap) without generating anything; confirm the
        spend with the user, then call again with confirm=true to actually
        dispatch generation. The finished artifact can be scheduled with
        schedule_aiv_artifacts; immediate publishing stays in the app, see
        get_app_link("aiv_artifact", ...).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            prompt: The AI Visibility prompt text to generate an article for.
            topic_id: Optional key-topic id this prompt belongs to.
            keyword_id: Optional tracked Keyword id this prompt is derived from.
            confirm: Must be true to actually generate; false (default) previews.

tools.name: start_ranklink_discovery
tools.description:
Start a RankLink silo-discovery run. SPENDS SILO QUOTA and triggers
        paid AI generation (queued, completes asynchronously).

        Call get_generation_quota first to check the remaining silo budget
        (quota.ranklink_silos). Leave confirm at its default (false) to preview
        (quota + today's cap) without starting anything; confirm with the user,
        then call again with confirm=true to actually start discovery. Use
        get_ranklink_discovery_status to poll. Approving/publishing discovered
        silos is NOT available here — that's done in the app, see
        get_app_link("ranklink", ...).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            confirm: Must be true to actually start; false (default) previews.

tools.name: run_direct_visibility_scan
tools.description:
Run an on-demand Direct Visibility scan (measures how often LLMs cite
        the site). Triggers paid AI generation (queued, completes asynchronously).
        PRODUCTION ONLY — refused in every other environment.

        Leave confirm at its default (false) to preview today's cap without
        starting anything; confirm with the user, then call again with
        confirm=true to actually start the scan. Use get_dv_dashboard /
        get_dv_trend to check results once it completes.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            track: "market" (default) or "content".
            confirm: Must be true to actually run; false (default) previews.

tools.name: schedule_blogs
tools.description:
Schedule one or more blog posts to publish on a future date.

        Sets the publish date without touching the CMS — the auto-publisher
        pushes each post live when its scheduled time arrives (checked a few
        times a day, so timing is approximate). Only draft/scheduled posts are
        eligible; already-published/archived ids come back in ``skipped``. This
        does NOT publish immediately — immediate publishing is an in-app action.

        Provide either ``date`` (all posts get the same day) or ``spread=True``
        (posts are spread evenly across the remaining billing cycle). ``date``
        is a calendar date ``YYYY-MM-DD`` (interpreted at midnight in your
        account timezone) or an ISO-8601 datetime with an explicit offset; the
        response echoes the resolved local date so you can confirm it matches
        what the app shows.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            blog_ids: Blog post ids (UUIDs) to schedule — see list_blogs.
            date: Target date (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO-8601). Required unless spread.
            spread: Spread evenly across the remaining billing cycle instead of
                a single date.

tools.name: schedule_aiv_artifacts
tools.description:
Schedule one or more AI Visibility (GEO) artifacts to publish later.

        Same behavior as schedule_blogs, scoped to GEO artifacts. Sets the
        publish date only; the CMS push happens automatically at the scheduled
        time. Publishing an artifact right now is an in-app action. Only
        draft/scheduled artifacts are eligible; others come back in ``skipped``.

        Provide either ``date`` (same day for all) or ``spread=True`` (spread
        across the remaining billing cycle). ``date`` is ``YYYY-MM-DD``
        (account-timezone midnight) or an ISO-8601 datetime with an offset.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            artifact_ids: Artifact ids (UUIDs) to schedule — see list_blogs
                (Blog.type == "artifact").
            date: Target date (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO-8601). Required unless spread.
            spread: Spread evenly across the remaining billing cycle instead of
                a single date.

tools.name: get_subscription_status
tools.description:
Get a project's current subscription status (read-only).

        Reports whether the subscription is active, whether it will renew or is
        set to cancel at period end (`will_cancel`), the period end date, and
        days remaining.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: list_dns_records
tools.description:
List the DNS records of an Edge SEO (NS-delegated) project's zone.

        Returns ``{records, total, truncated}``. Each record carries
        ``managed_by_us`` / ``protected`` flags: protected rows (Cloudflare-
        managed records, apex authority records, and the Edge-managed apex/www
        web records) cannot be deleted and mostly cannot be edited. Projects
        without an onboarded Edge SEO zone return an empty list.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: create_dns_record
tools.description:
Create a DNS record in an Edge SEO (NS-delegated) project's zone.

        Requires a connected Edge SEO zone; other projects fail with
        EDGE_NOT_CONNECTED. Supported types: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, CAA,
        SRV, NS. ``name`` accepts ``@`` or empty for the apex, a relative
        label (``shop``, ``_sip._tcp``), or an absolute name inside the zone.
        SRV/CAA use ``data`` instead of ``content`` (SRV:
        ``{priority, weight, port, target}``; CAA: ``{flags, tag, value}``).
        Proxy is forced on for the apex/www web record, never proxied for
        non-web types, and rejected for wildcard/underscore-label names;
        otherwise it follows ``proxied`` (default DNS-only). Creating a CAA
        record at the apex/www needs ``acknowledge_edge_impact=true`` (can
        break Universal SSL issuance); apex/www NS records cannot be created.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            record_type: One of A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, CAA, SRV, NS.
            name: Record name — ``@``/empty for apex, relative label, or
                absolute name within the project's domain.
            content: Record value (IP, hostname, or text; max 2048 chars).
                Unused for SRV/CAA (use ``data`` instead).
            priority: MX priority 0-65535 (defaults to 10; ignored for
                non-MX types).
            ttl: Integer 1 (Auto) or 60-86400; omitted defaults to Auto.
            proxied: Cloudflare proxy toggle for A/AAAA/CNAME (default false).
            data: Structured payload for SRV/CAA.
            acknowledge_edge_impact: Required true to create a CAA record at
                the apex/www.

tools.name: update_dns_record
tools.description:
Update one DNS record in place; the record's type is immutable.

        Requires a connected Edge SEO zone. Cloudflare-managed rows and the
        zone's apex/www NS records cannot be edited. The Edge-managed
        apex/www web record cannot be renamed, and its content/origin (and
        any CAA record at the apex/www) needs
        ``acknowledge_edge_impact=true`` to change.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            record_id: The DNS record id (32-hex, from list_dns_records).
            name: New record name (same rules as create_dns_record).
            content: New record value (max 2048 chars); unused for SRV/CAA.
            priority: MX priority 0-65535 (ignored for non-MX types).
            ttl: Integer 1 (Auto) or 60-86400; omitted defaults to Auto.
            proxied: Cloudflare proxy toggle for A/AAAA/CNAME.
            data: Structured payload for SRV/CAA.
            acknowledge_edge_impact: Required true for Edge-managed web
                record content changes or any apex/www CAA edit.

tools.name: delete_dns_record
tools.description:
Delete one DNS record from an Edge SEO (NS-delegated) project's zone.

        Requires a connected Edge SEO zone. Cloudflare-managed rows and the
        zone's apex/www NS records cannot be deleted. Deleting the
        Edge-managed apex/www web record needs
        ``acknowledge_edge_impact=true`` AND another A/AAAA/CNAME record for
        that exact host — the last one serving the site can never be
        deleted, so this cannot break the Edge SEO setup itself. Record ids
        only ever resolve against this project's own zone. Returns
        ``{deleted: true}`` (also for ids that no longer exist).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            record_id: The DNS record id (32-hex, from list_dns_records).
            acknowledge_edge_impact: Required true to delete an Edge-managed
                web record or an apex/www CAA record.

                suggestions.

tools.name: list_recommendations
tools.description:
List a project's SEO recommendations, grouped by status.

        Returns approved/archived/declined/resolved/deleting/deleted
        buckets (newly-generated, not-yet-reviewed recommendations aren't
        included here — see get_recommendations_count for the full status
        breakdown, including "new"). To approve a recommendation use
        approve_recommendation / approve_all_recommendations; publishing the
        approved fix to the live site happens via an async snippet-regen job
        (no separate "publish" step in the app for this either).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            sub_category: Optional filter, e.g. "keyword-cannibalization".
            search: Optional case-insensitive text search over the recommendation content.

tools.name: get_recommendations_count
tools.description:
Get recommendation counts by status/sub-category for a project (dashboard summary).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: approve_recommendation
tools.description:
Approve a single SEO recommendation.

        Approving only marks intent, same as in the app — the live CMS/site
        picks up the change via an async snippet-regen job, it isn't a
        separate "publish" step you need to trigger.

        Args:
            recommendation_id: The recommendation's id (UUID) — see list_recommendations.

tools.name: approve_all_recommendations
tools.description:
Approve every pending SEO recommendation for a project (optionally filtered).

        Same as the app's "Fix All" button. Approving only marks intent — the
        live site picks up approved fixes via an async snippet-regen job.

        keyword-cannibalization is never auto-approved here: fixing it rewrites
        live keyphrases across multiple pages and requires choosing which page
        keeps the keyword, so that always needs human review in the app (this
        call returns a refusal with a deep link instead of approving).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            sub_category: Optional filter, e.g. "title" or "schema-markup".
                Omit to approve everything (including schema markup).

tools.name: get_integration_status
tools.description:
Check which CMS/analytics integrations are connected for a project.

        Returns a connected bool per provider (wordpress, shopify, wix,
        webflow, gohighlevel, gsc) plus an app_links block pointing every
        disconnected provider at the Integrations page. Google Search Console
        and WordPress can start browser authorization via MCP; integrations
        that require pasted credentials must be connected in the app.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: start_gsc_connect
tools.description:
Start a Google Search Console connect flow for a project.

        This only returns a Google consent URL — it does NOT complete the
        connection. The human user must open the URL in a browser and finish
        Google's sign-in/consent screen themselves; there is no way to
        complete this flow programmatically. After they finish, call
        get_integration_status to confirm gsc is connected.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: start_wordpress_connect
tools.description:
Start the WordPress auto-install connect flow for a project.

        Returns a URL to the site's WP admin "Authorize Application" page.
        This does NOT complete the connection — the human user must open the
        URL in a browser and approve the authorization themselves. After
        they finish, call get_integration_status to confirm wordpress is
        connected. Only works for websites detected as WordPress; other
        platforms should use their browser setup tool or get_app_link.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: start_gohighlevel_connect
tools.description:
Get the secure browser link for GoHighLevel setup.

        This does not change any integration state. The human user must open
        the RankAuthority Integrations page and complete setup there; the AI
        cannot request or receive credentials in chat.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: start_webflow_connect
tools.description:
Get the secure browser link for Webflow setup.

        This does not change any integration state. The project owner must
        open the RankAuthority Integrations page and complete setup there; the
        AI cannot request or receive credentials in chat.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: start_shopify_connect
tools.description:
Get the secure browser link for Shopify setup.

        This does not change any integration state. The project owner must
        open the RankAuthority Integrations page and complete setup there; the
        AI cannot request or receive credentials in chat.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: start_wix_connect
tools.description:
Get the secure browser link for Wix setup.

        This does not change any integration state. The project owner must
        open the RankAuthority Integrations page and complete setup there; the
        AI cannot request or receive credentials in chat.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: get_app_link
tools.description:
Get a deep link into the RankAuthority web app for a fenced-off action.

        Call this whenever the user asks for something this MCP surface
        doesn't expose as a tool — immediate publishing, entering integration
        credentials, disconnecting an integration, running a fresh scan,
        bulk actions, or an AI keyword search — then present the returned URL
        so they can finish the action in the app.

        Args:
            action: One of "blog_publish", "rankfast", "aiv_artifact",
                "ranklink", "integrations", "scan", "ai_keyword_search",
                "direct_visibility".
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID) to scope the link to.

        Returns:
            {"url": ..., "instructions": ...} on success, or
            {"error": ..., "known_actions": [...]} if `action` is unrecognized.

tools.name: list_blogs
tools.description:
List a project's blog posts (paginated, newest first).

        Covers both blogs and AI Visibility artifacts (``Blog.type``), draft
        through published. Generating new blog content is done via the
        generate_blog tool; scheduling a draft's publish date is done via
        schedule_blogs / schedule_aiv_artifacts. Publishing immediately is an
        in-app action — see get_app_link("blog_publish", ...).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            status: Optional filter — "draft", "scheduled", "published",
                "consolidated", or "archived".

tools.name: get_blog_generation_status
tools.description:
List a project's in-progress blog generation queue items.

        Only returns rows still pending/started/generating — once a blog
        finishes generating it moves out of this queue and shows up in
        list_blogs instead.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: list_rankfast_pages
tools.description:
List a project's RankFast campaigns (pages with generated content).

        Returns every RankFast row that already has generated content
        (new/pending/approved/scheduled/published/archived), newest first.
        Generating RankFast content for a fresh page is done via
        generate_rankfast; publishing or scheduling an existing draft is done
        in the app — see get_app_link("rankfast", ...).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: get_rankfast_counts
tools.description:
Get RankFast campaign counts by status for a project (dashboard summary).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: get_aiv_dashboard
tools.description:
Get the AI Visibility dashboard for a project: latest record + persona/topic/prompt counts.

        Immediate publishing of a generated GEO artifact is done in the app —
        see get_app_link("aiv_artifact", ...). Generate a new artifact with
        generate_aiv_artifact, or schedule one with schedule_aiv_artifacts;
        call get_generation_quota first to check the remaining article budget.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: list_aiv_prompts
tools.description:
List a project's active AI Visibility prompts (the queries GEO artifacts answer).

        These are the prompts you can grow with add_aiv_prompts — a good AI-
        assisted workflow is to draft new buyer-intent prompts yourself and add
        them here. Personas and key topics are managed only in the app.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: add_aiv_prompts
tools.description:
Add one or more AI Visibility prompts to a project (plain insert; no AI cost).

        Each new prompt consumes one slot from the plan's AIV prompt budget.
        This does NOT run any AI generation — draft the prompt text yourself (or
        with the assistant) and add it. Pass a single-item list to add just one.
        To generate a GEO artifact from prompts, use generate_aiv_artifact.

        Duplicates (case-insensitive) — already present or repeated within the
        list — are skipped and reported in ``skipped_duplicates``, not errors.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            prompts: The prompt/query texts to track (1 or more).
            related_topic: Optional topic label applied to every added prompt.

tools.name: delete_aiv_prompts
tools.description:
Delete one or more AI Visibility prompts from a project.

        Pass a single-item list to delete just one. Each successful delete
        refunds one prompt slot. Prompts already linked to a generated artifact
        or blog cannot be deleted and are reported in ``blocked``; unknown ids
        land in ``not_found``.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            prompt_ids: The prompt ids (UUIDs) to delete — see list_aiv_prompts.

tools.name: get_dv_dashboard
tools.description:
Get the latest Direct Visibility run summary for a project.

        Direct Visibility measures how often LLMs cite the site in response
        to real queries. "market" track uses top keywords by AI search
        volume; "content" track uses the project's own AI Visibility prompts.
        Run a fresh scan with run_direct_visibility_scan.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            track: "market" (default) or "content".

tools.name: get_dv_trend
tools.description:
Get historical Direct Visibility runs for a project (trend chart data).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            track: "market" (default) or "content".
            limit: Max number of most-recent runs to return (1-24, default 6).

tools.name: get_dv_queries
tools.description:
Get per-query citation results for a Direct Visibility run (defaults to the latest run).

        Content-track results are enriched with the linked blog's publish
        state (content_status, scheduled_date, published_date).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            track: "market" (default) or "content".
            run_id: Specific run id (UUID) to inspect; omit for the latest run.

tools.name: get_ranklink_dashboard
tools.description:
Get the RankLink dashboard for a project: silo/proposal/page counts.

        Discovering new silos is done via start_ranklink_discovery; publishing
        an approved silo's internal links to the live CMS is done in the app —
        see get_app_link("ranklink", ...).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: list_ranklink_silos
tools.description:
List a project's RankLink silos (topic clusters + orphan-recovery groups).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: get_ranklink_discovery_status
tools.description:
Get the most recent RankLink silo-discovery run's status (for polling).

        Does not include the discovered silos themselves — call
        list_ranklink_silos once the run's status is "completed".

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: get_generation_quota
tools.description:
Get a project's remaining generation quota across every content domain.

        ALWAYS call this before offering to generate a blog, RankFast page,
        or AI Visibility artifact, so you can tell the user up front if the
        relevant quota is exhausted instead of letting generate_* fail. Each
        domain's ``remaining`` is the exact count the app itself enforces
        (no separate math here) — 0 means generation for that domain will be
        rejected until the quota resets.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: generate_blog
tools.description:
Generate a new blog post for a keyword. SPENDS BLOG QUOTA and triggers
        paid AI generation (queued, completes asynchronously).

        Call get_generation_quota first to check the remaining blog budget. This
        tool itself is safe to call with confirm left at its default (false) —
        it only returns a preview (quota + today's cap) without generating
        anything. Confirm the spend with the user, then call again with
        confirm=true to actually queue generation. The finished draft can be
        scheduled with schedule_blogs; immediate publishing stays in the app,
        see get_app_link("blog_publish", ...).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            keyword: The keyword/topic to write the blog post about.
            keyword_id: Optional id of an existing tracked Keyword row to associate.
            confirm: Must be true to actually generate; false (default) previews.

tools.name: generate_rankfast
tools.description:
Generate RankFast content for chosen blog pages. SPENDS RANKFAST QUOTA
        and triggers paid AI generation (queued, completes asynchronously).

        Call get_generation_quota first to check the remaining RankFast budget.
        Leave confirm at its default (false) to preview (quota + today's cap)
        without generating anything; confirm the spend with the user, then call
        again with confirm=true to actually dispatch generation.
        Publishing/scheduling the finished content is NOT available here —
        that's done in the app, see get_app_link("rankfast", ...).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            page_ids: Page ids (UUID, see list_rankfast_pages / the app) to
                generate RankFast content for. Non-blog or unknown ids are
                skipped, not errored.
            confirm: Must be true to actually generate; false (default) previews.

tools.name: generate_aiv_artifact
tools.description:
Generate one AI Visibility (GEO) article for a prompt. SPENDS ARTICLE
        QUOTA and triggers paid AI generation (queued, completes asynchronously).

        Call get_generation_quota first to check the remaining AIV article
        budget (quota.aiv.article). Leave confirm at its default (false) to
        preview (quota + today's cap) without generating anything; confirm the
        spend with the user, then call again with confirm=true to actually
        dispatch generation. The finished artifact can be scheduled with
        schedule_aiv_artifacts; immediate publishing stays in the app, see
        get_app_link("aiv_artifact", ...).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            prompt: The AI Visibility prompt text to generate an article for.
            topic_id: Optional key-topic id this prompt belongs to.
            keyword_id: Optional tracked Keyword id this prompt is derived from.
            confirm: Must be true to actually generate; false (default) previews.

tools.name: start_ranklink_discovery
tools.description:
Start a RankLink silo-discovery run. SPENDS SILO QUOTA and triggers
        paid AI generation (queued, completes asynchronously).

        Call get_generation_quota first to check the remaining silo budget
        (quota.ranklink_silos). Leave confirm at its default (false) to preview
        (quota + today's cap) without starting anything; confirm with the user,
        then call again with confirm=true to actually start discovery. Use
        get_ranklink_discovery_status to poll. Approving/publishing discovered
        silos is NOT available here — that's done in the app, see
        get_app_link("ranklink", ...).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            confirm: Must be true to actually start; false (default) previews.

tools.name: run_direct_visibility_scan
tools.description:
Run an on-demand Direct Visibility scan (measures how often LLMs cite
        the site). Triggers paid AI generation (queued, completes asynchronously).
        PRODUCTION ONLY — refused in every other environment.

        Leave confirm at its default (false) to preview today's cap without
        starting anything; confirm with the user, then call again with
        confirm=true to actually start the scan. Use get_dv_dashboard /
        get_dv_trend to check results once it completes.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            track: "market" (default) or "content".
            confirm: Must be true to actually run; false (default) previews.

tools.name: schedule_blogs
tools.description:
Schedule one or more blog posts to publish on a future date.

        Sets the publish date without touching the CMS — the auto-publisher
        pushes each post live when its scheduled time arrives (checked a few
        times a day, so timing is approximate). Only draft/scheduled posts are
        eligible; already-published/archived ids come back in ``skipped``. This
        does NOT publish immediately — immediate publishing is an in-app action.

        Provide either ``date`` (all posts get the same day) or ``spread=True``
        (posts are spread evenly across the remaining billing cycle). ``date``
        is a calendar date ``YYYY-MM-DD`` (interpreted at midnight in your
        account timezone) or an ISO-8601 datetime with an explicit offset; the
        response echoes the resolved local date so you can confirm it matches
        what the app shows.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            blog_ids: Blog post ids (UUIDs) to schedule — see list_blogs.
            date: Target date (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO-8601). Required unless spread.
            spread: Spread evenly across the remaining billing cycle instead of
                a single date.

tools.name: schedule_aiv_artifacts
tools.description:
Schedule one or more AI Visibility (GEO) artifacts to publish later.

        Same behavior as schedule_blogs, scoped to GEO artifacts. Sets the
        publish date only; the CMS push happens automatically at the scheduled
        time. Publishing an artifact right now is an in-app action. Only
        draft/scheduled artifacts are eligible; others come back in ``skipped``.

        Provide either ``date`` (same day for all) or ``spread=True`` (spread
        across the remaining billing cycle). ``date`` is ``YYYY-MM-DD``
        (account-timezone midnight) or an ISO-8601 datetime with an offset.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            artifact_ids: Artifact ids (UUIDs) to schedule — see list_blogs
                (Blog.type == "artifact").
            date: Target date (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO-8601). Required unless spread.
            spread: Spread evenly across the remaining billing cycle instead of
                a single date.

tools.name: get_subscription_status
tools.description:
Get a project's current subscription status (read-only).

        Reports whether the subscription is active, whether it will renew or is
        set to cancel at period end (`will_cancel`), the period end date, and
        days remaining.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: list_dns_records
tools.description:
List the DNS records of an Edge SEO (NS-delegated) project's zone.

        Returns ``{records, total, truncated}``. Each record carries
        ``managed_by_us`` / ``protected`` flags: protected rows (Cloudflare-
        managed records, apex authority records, and the Edge-managed apex/www
        web records) cannot be deleted and mostly cannot be edited. Projects
        without an onboarded Edge SEO zone return an empty list.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).

tools.name: create_dns_record
tools.description:
Create a DNS record in an Edge SEO (NS-delegated) project's zone.

        Requires a connected Edge SEO zone; other projects fail with
        EDGE_NOT_CONNECTED. Supported types: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, CAA,
        SRV, NS. ``name`` accepts ``@`` or empty for the apex, a relative
        label (``shop``, ``_sip._tcp``), or an absolute name inside the zone.
        SRV/CAA use ``data`` instead of ``content`` (SRV:
        ``{priority, weight, port, target}``; CAA: ``{flags, tag, value}``).
        Proxy is forced on for the apex/www web record, never proxied for
        non-web types, and rejected for wildcard/underscore-label names;
        otherwise it follows ``proxied`` (default DNS-only). Creating a CAA
        record at the apex/www needs ``acknowledge_edge_impact=true`` (can
        break Universal SSL issuance); apex/www NS records cannot be created.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            record_type: One of A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, CAA, SRV, NS.
            name: Record name — ``@``/empty for apex, relative label, or
                absolute name within the project's domain.
            content: Record value (IP, hostname, or text; max 2048 chars).
                Unused for SRV/CAA (use ``data`` instead).
            priority: MX priority 0-65535 (defaults to 10; ignored for
                non-MX types).
            ttl: Integer 1 (Auto) or 60-86400; omitted defaults to Auto.
            proxied: Cloudflare proxy toggle for A/AAAA/CNAME (default false).
            data: Structured payload for SRV/CAA.
            acknowledge_edge_impact: Required true to create a CAA record at
                the apex/www.

tools.name: update_dns_record
tools.description:
Update one DNS record in place; the record's type is immutable.

        Requires a connected Edge SEO zone. Cloudflare-managed rows and the
        zone's apex/www NS records cannot be edited. The Edge-managed
        apex/www web record cannot be renamed, and its content/origin (and
        any CAA record at the apex/www) needs
        ``acknowledge_edge_impact=true`` to change.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            record_id: The DNS record id (32-hex, from list_dns_records).
            name: New record name (same rules as create_dns_record).
            content: New record value (max 2048 chars); unused for SRV/CAA.
            priority: MX priority 0-65535 (ignored for non-MX types).
            ttl: Integer 1 (Auto) or 60-86400; omitted defaults to Auto.
            proxied: Cloudflare proxy toggle for A/AAAA/CNAME.
            data: Structured payload for SRV/CAA.
            acknowledge_edge_impact: Required true for Edge-managed web
                record content changes or any apex/www CAA edit.

tools.name: delete_dns_record
tools.description:
Delete one DNS record from an Edge SEO (NS-delegated) project's zone.

        Requires a connected Edge SEO zone. Cloudflare-managed rows and the
        zone's apex/www NS records cannot be deleted. Deleting the
        Edge-managed apex/www web record needs
        ``acknowledge_edge_impact=true`` AND another A/AAAA/CNAME record for
        that exact host — the last one serving the site can never be
        deleted, so this cannot break the Edge SEO setup itself. Record ids
        only ever resolve against this project's own zone. Returns
        ``{deleted: true}`` (also for ids that no longer exist).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            record_id: The DNS record id (32-hex, from list_dns_records).
            acknowledge_edge_impact: Required true to delete an Edge-managed
                web record or an apex/www CAA record.

flags.description:
Approve AI-suggested keywords, moving them into active tracking.

        Approving charges the project's keyword budget (same as add_keywords)
        and queues the same DataForSEO metric tracking for each approved
        keyword.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            suggestion_ids: Specific suggestion ids to approve (see
                list_keyword_suggestions), or omit to approve all pending
                suggestions.
flags.hypothesis: Broad language may route a narrow task to an unnecessarily large response; bounded semantics may explain this language.

flags.description:
Reject AI-suggested keywords, deleting them without charging the budget.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            suggestion_ids: Specific suggestion ids to reject (see
                list_keyword_suggestions), or omit to reject all pending
                suggestions.
flags.hypothesis: Broad language may route a narrow task to an unnecessarily large response; bounded semantics may explain this language.

flags.description:
Approve every pending SEO recommendation for a project (optionally filtered).

        Same as the app's "Fix All" button. Approving only marks intent — the
        live site picks up approved fixes via an async snippet-regen job.

        keyword-cannibalization is never auto-approved here: fixing it rewrites
        live keyphrases across multiple pages and requires choosing which page
        keeps the keyword, so that always needs human review in the app (this
        call returns a refusal with a deep link instead of approving).

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            sub_category: Optional filter, e.g. "title" or "schema-markup".
                Omit to approve everything (including schema markup).

flags.description:
Schedule one or more blog posts to publish on a future date.

        Sets the publish date without touching the CMS — the auto-publisher
        pushes each post live when its scheduled time arrives (checked a few
        times a day, so timing is approximate). Only draft/scheduled posts are
        eligible; already-published/archived ids come back in ``skipped``. This
        does NOT publish immediately — immediate publishing is an in-app action.

        Provide either ``date`` (all posts get the same day) or ``spread=True``
        (posts are spread evenly across the remaining billing cycle). ``date``
        is a calendar date ``YYYY-MM-DD`` (interpreted at midnight in your
        account timezone) or an ISO-8601 datetime with an explicit offset; the
        response echoes the resolved local date so you can confirm it matches
        what the app shows.

        Args:
            website_id: The project's website id (UUID).
            blog_ids: Blog post ids (UUIDs) to schedule — see list_blogs.
            date: Target date (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO-8601). Required unless spread.
            spread: Spread evenly across the remaining billing cycle instead of
                a single date.
flags.hypothesis: Broad language may route a narrow task to an unnecessarily large response; bounded semantics may explain this language.

            date: Target date (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO-8601). Required unless spread.
            spread: Spread evenly across the remaining billing cycle instead of
